To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the establishment of a new PTA or the expansion of a pre-existing one increases the likelihood of a pair of countries entering a bilateral PTA; and the impact is larger when members of the new or expanded PTAs are on the average geographically closer to the pair of non-member countries.
the impact of preexisting PTAs on the probability of a country-pair entering a PTA is larger when the pre-existing PTAs include members that are geographically closer to the country-pair.
pre-existing PTA memberships increase the probability that countries will join a PTA and this effect is stronger for pairs of countries that are geographically close.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how PTAs are established and how they affect the formation of new PTAs.
how the incentives of countries to enter PTAs are influenced by the actions of other countries.
the interdependencies that arise from the proliferation of PTAs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the probability of a country pair entering a bilateral PTA increases with the number of pre-existing PTAS and that the effect diminishes with geographical distance.

PTAs have a positive effect in the sense that the probability of a country-pair entering into a PTA is positively correlated with the number of existing PTAs, and this correlation is larger when the countries in the pair are geographically close.
the probability of two countries entering into a preferential trade agreement is higher when they are closer to each other and when there is a pre-existing agreement among their neighbors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the probability of a country-pair entering a bilateral PTA increases with the number of existing PTAs to which they belong and that this effect is larger the closer these PTAs are geographically to the pair of potential members.
PTAs are interdependent and this interdependence increases with geographical proximity.

the probability of a new PTA being established depends on whether the countries are geographically close, whether they have existing PTAs, and whether they are geographically close to countries with PTAs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PTAs are not isolated events.
the establishment of a new PTA or an expansion of an existing PTA can have a significant effect on the formation of a new PTC.
PTAs are interdependent and that PTAs are more likely to be formed with nearby countries.
